subject: Model fit evals & tool-calling: JSON schema follow-up

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 09:02:00 -0800
Subject: Model fit evals & tool-calling: post-call notes and next steps

Hi Claire / Arjun —

Thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and recommended next steps so we have alignment: 

- Goal: validate model fit for Finadata's document ingestion use case (structured extraction + downstream joins). Primary success criteria are JSON schema compliance (strict field names + types), latency under 350ms p50 for short docs, and >=95% extraction accuracy on the seed prompt set.
- Risks you called out: strict schema validation failures today, intermittent retries when function calls time out, and cost sensitivity around 24/7 inference.

Next steps (what I'll coordinate):
1) Share our recommended model variants and a prompt set for your evals (attached).
2) Run a 72-hour bench with suggested batching/quantization settings and share the benchmark CSV.
3) Work with Marissa/Rishi on JSON schema compliance tests (tool-calling retries, deterministic outputs).
4) Schedule a follow-up to review results and decide on Dedicated vs Hosted routing.

I've attached the prompt set and will ask Rishi for a short tech note on retries and structured-output stability. Proposed timing: bench kickoff Wednesday, results by end of Friday. Does that work for your side?

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Claire Johnson <claire@finadata.com>

Subject: Re: Model fit evals & tool-calling: post-call notes and next steps

Hi Vanessa —

Thanks for the recap, that looks right. A couple clarifying points from our side:
- We need the JSON schema to be strict — nulls not allowed for some top-level fields and arrays must always be present (empty array ok).
- For function/tool calling, our ingestion pipeline currently retries once before marking a document for manual review; we'd like to avoid increasing that.
- Can you include recommended retry/backoff settings and any model-level config to improve deterministic outputs (e.g., temperature=0.0, top_p adjustments)?

Wednesday kickoff is fine. I'll loop in our SRE (Arjun) if we need to coordinate VPC/network keys for Dedicated testing.

—Claire
Head of Data Products, Finadata

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 13:33:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Fwd: Model fit evals & tool-calling: post-call notes and next steps

Vanessa / Marissa —

See recommended package below (sending as a single note so Vanessa can forward to Claire):

Recommended models & config:
1) redwood-lite-8k (fast/low-cost) — quantized int4, batching=auto (max batch 32), temp=0.0, top_p=0.8. Expected p50 latency: ~180-250ms on gpus with NVLink. Good for high throughput but lower extraction nuance.
2) redwood-balanced-16k (balanced) — 8-bit quantization, batching=auto (max batch 16), temp=0.0, top_p=0.6. Expected p50 latency: ~280-360ms. Best tradeoff for schema correctness + cost.
3) redwood-accurate-16k-raw (high-quality) — no quant, temp=0.0, top_p=0.4, batching=manual (batch size 8 for lowest variance). Expected p50 latency: ~380-480ms. Use for edge-case docs and final QA.

JSON schema and tool-calling notes:
- Schema strictness: we recommend using the runtime's structured-output validator with 'strict' mode on. It will reject non-conforming outputs rather than silently coerce. For fields that cannot be null, add required:true in the schema.
- Retries: keep application-layer retry=1 (your current), but at the runtime set function call timeout to 2s and enable idempotency keys so duplicate calls don't cause double-processing. We saw in prior customers that increasing retries increases manual review rate.
- Determinism: set temperature=0.0 and top_p <=0.6 for extraction; enable max_output_tokens to guard truncation. Also lock model version for the benchmark run to avoid drift.
- Structured-output failures: we expect ~2-6% initial schema failures on edge docs. Two mitigations: (a) preprocessing normalization (whitespace, bullet normalization) and (b) a small post-processor that maps common misspellings to schema fields before failing.

Bench plan & artifacts attached: eval_benchmarks_20270110.csv is the template for metrics (p50/p95 latency, tokens, schema-failure-rate, retries, cost-per-doc). Finadata_prompt_set_v1.json is the 150-doc seed set you asked for.

Quick troubleshooting checklist (if they see schema flakiness):
- Confirm model and quantization variant are locked during the run.
- Check for truncated outputs (increase max_output_tokens).
- If tool-calls are timing out, increase the function timeout to 2.5s temporarily and log the payload size.

I'll attach the two files and the SOC2 artifact request Claire asked for. If you want, I can also run an initial 50-doc smoke run on Hosted and share results this afternoon.

—Rishi
Sr. Applied ML Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>

Claire / Arjun —

Attaching the seed prompt set and benchmark template (also uploaded here: https://drive.google.com/finadata/prompt-set). Rishi included the recommended model variants and deterministic settings; key callouts inline below: 

- Start with redwood-balanced-16k, temp=0.0, top_p=0.6, batching=auto(max 16). This gives the best chance to meet schema fidelity without blowing cost.
- Keep your app retry=1. We'll set function-call timeout=2s and enable idempotency keys so retries don't cause duplication.
- If you see >6% schema failures in the first 100 docs, switch to redwood-accurate-16k-raw for just those failing classes and we'll analyze common failure modes.

Next steps / schedule: 
- Wed 13 Jan 09:00 PST: kickoff bench (you can start anytime today; we recommend starting before noon).
- Fri 15 Jan EOD: Redwood shares completed CSV with p50/p95, schema-failure-rate, retries, and cost-per-doc.
- Mon 18 Jan: review call to decide routing (Dedicated vs Hosted).

Attachments: Finadata_prompt_set_v1.json, eval_benchmarks_20270110.csv, SOC2_artifact_request.pdf

If that timeline works I'll send a calendar invite for the Monday review now.
\Best —
Vanessa Ortiz
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
